## Bio

*[Adriano
Rutz]{about="wd:Q97455964" property="wdt:P31" resource="wd:Q5" typeof="schema:Person"}*
is a [postdoctoral
researcher]{about="wd:Q1125292" property="wdt:P31" resource="wd:Q28640" typeof="schema:Occupation"}
at [ETH
Zürich]{about="wd:Q11942" property="wdt:P31" resource="wd:Q875538" typeof="schema:CollegeOrUniversity"},
where he develops [computational]{about="wd:Q104595152"} and [analytical
methods]{about="wd:Q4751159"} for [metabolomics]{about="wd:Q12149006"}. His
research{about="wd:Q42240"} focuses on the chemistry{about="wd:Q2329"} of
Life{about="wd:Q3"} and the metabolites{about="wd:Q407595"} found in
organisms{about="wd:Q7239"}. He trained in pharmaceutical sciences and
phytochemistry, worked at Tradall SA (Bacardi Group), and completed his PhD at
the University of Geneva.

His work uses mass spectrometry to determine which metabolites are present in a
sample, and aims to make this knowledge open and reusable. He is a core
contributor to the [LOTUS initiative](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.70780), an
open resource linking metabolites to the organisms in which they are found, and
works across data science, chemistry, and biology.
